title: Neural labeling and manipulation by neonatal intraventricular viral injection in mice
protocol: Separate the whole litter of pups from the mother and place onto a heated pad (∼35°C) next to the injection setup.
Add bedding and nesting material to ensure comfort and to enable pups to retain maternal smell.
Place one neonate inside the falcon tube padded with tissue paper and close the lid tightly.
Close the lid tightly in order to quickly achieve a high concentration of vaporized isoflurane.
Observe closely for the moment the pup stops struggling and immediately take it out.
Test anesthesia by light toe pinching.
If you get a reaction, put it back for an additional 10 s of anesthesia.
Minimize anesthetizing time for neonatal mice.
Take care that pups do not come into direct contact with liquid isoflurane to avoid skin irritation.
Fix pup on the injection stage with tape.
Cover pup’s head with ample ultrasound gel.
Find lateral ventricle for injection.
Dip ultrasound head into ultrasound gel covering the mouse pup.
Lower ultrasound head until live images of brain structures appear on the ultrasound screen.
Move ultrasound head laterally to find the injection plane where the ventricle appears largest.
Align head of ultrasound device with previously mounted injection needle.
Adjust the needle to approach the head in y-direction until the tip is dipped in ultrasound gel under the ultrasound head and near the skull.
Move the microinjection needle in x-direction until it aligns with the correct ultrasound plane and becomes focused on the ultrasound screen.
Penetrate the pup’s skull until the tip of the micropipette reaches the lateral ventricle.
Retract the micropipette if a dent occurs to allow the skull to regain its proper shape.
Inject up to 3 μL of viral solution into the lateral ventricle at a flux rate of 30 nL/s.
Withdraw injection needle after injection.
Recover injected mice by gently removing remaining ultrasound gel from pups with soft tissue.
Place the pup on a heating pad at approximately 35°C.
Return the pup to the mother only when it is fully awake and shows healthy pink skin coloring.
Monitor for expression of fluorescent proteins, detectable as early as 3 days post injection in peripheral and central nervous systems.
Quantify the percentage of TdTomato positive cells relative to NeuroTrace stained neurons in various brain regions.
Perform the injection as quickly as possible, ensuring the process takes no more than 5 minutes per mouse pup.
Ensure that the injection flux rate does not exceed 30 nL/s to prevent increased intracranial pressure.
Replace the microinjection needle if skin bleeding occurs during injection.
Tattoo mouse pups on paws for identification (optional).
Obtain tail biopsies from mouse pups for genotyping if required (optional).
Offer oral analgesia such as Meloxicam (∼5 μg per pup, e.g., 10 μL of 0.5 μg/μL solution) to the mouse pups (optional).
